intended_application: Offer Waymo-operated on-demand passenger trips in Phoenix within Waymo's confirmed service area as an alternative to human-driven rides
organization: Phoenix Civic Mobility Office, a fictional municipal mobility provider used solely as a decision case
business_need: Improve late-evening trip availability while retaining access for riders who need disability accommodations
users_stakeholders: Adult riders, riders with disabilities, public officials, Waymo, customer support, insurers, road users, Arizona regulators
adoption_posture: Conservative and risk-averse: requires stronger proof of equitable access, oversight and liability clarity before any public passenger pilot
capabilities_constraints: Can study travel gaps and run tabletop exercises, but has no confirmed Waymo agreement, procurement authority, permit responsibility, accessible fleet equivalence, service-level guarantee, or incident-response terms
risk_consequence_context: Public trust, passenger/road-user injury, exclusion of riders with accessibility needs, procurement challenge, liability and service continuity; high reputational consequence
management_question: Should the municipal provider offer Waymo-operated taxi-like trips now as part of its public service?
time_horizon: Decision in October 2026; reassess in 6 months
additional_context: Fictional case. Keep the same Waymo evidence cutoff as the primary case. This contrast is intentionally similar in technology and passenger application but changes public obligations, consequences and adoption posture.
